title.value: Run parallel Operator sessions for car hunting and email

introduction.value: Chris Koerner ran several Operator sessions at once; he says it found undervalued cars by comparing KBB and NADA values and cut his email time by 80%.

method.value: Chris Koerner used the ChatGPT Pro plan ($200/month) to run Operator in many browser tabs at once. He says he had 6 running concurrently and did 10 different tasks. One task was finding undervalued cars by KBB and NADA values. Others included Airbnb and flight searches and scraping Chamber of Commerce sites for emails. The email-time cut he cites came from Lindy, a separate tool.

outcome.value: He says the car search worked and calls the result floor-flooring. He doesn't give numbers for it. He doesn't think Operator is worth $200/month for running a business yet, because it needs more finessing.

notes.value: The 80% email saving came from Lindy, not Operator. The newsletter gives details only in a linked YouTube video, so the written post is thin.

source_text.body:
Run parallel Operator sessions for car hunting and email
Chris Koerner ran several Operator sessions at once; he says it found undervalued cars by comparing KBB and NADA values and cut his email time by 80%.
Done with
OP
Operator
What they did
Chris Koerner used the ChatGPT Pro plan ($200/month) to run Operator in many browser tabs at once. He says he had 6 running concurrently and did 10 different tasks. One task was finding undervalued cars by KBB and NADA values. Others included Airbnb and flight searches and scraping Chamber of Commerce sites for emails. The email-time cut he cites came from Lindy, a separate tool.
How it went
He says the car search worked and calls the result floor-flooring. He doesn't give numbers for it. He doesn't think Operator is worth $200/month for running a business yet, because it needs more finessing.
Worth knowing
The 80% email saving came from Lindy, not Operator. The newsletter gives details only in a linked YouTube video, so the written post is thin.
Try it yourself
with
Operator
Copy prompt
I want to run two jobs in parallel. First, search [Kelley Blue Book and NADA, or other sites] and local listings for [car make/model, year range, price limit within [location]], and give me a shortlist of cars listed well below their estimated value, with links and the price gap. Second, go through my inbox at [email provider], summarize what needs a reply, and draft responses without sending anything. Stop when I have the shortlist and the drafts to review.
Original source: https://newsletter.chrisjkoerner.com/p/newsletter-00070-d548
